newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW - RTW acting to reverse weak Q4.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - RTW acting to reverse weak Q4.

text.p: RTW Inc, in the wake of disappointing fourth-quarter earnings on Thursday, said it will shore up its understaffed Denver operation and open a new office in Massachusetts, said David Prosser, chairman and president.

"We didn't react strongly enough to make changes in Denver, where claim and claim settlement expenses were higher than our expectations," Prosser said in an interview after noting that 50 percent of RTW's weaker quarterly performance was due to its understaffed Denver operation.
An increase in claim reserves in other parts of the country also hurt fourth quarter results.
During the quarter, Minneapolis-based RTW said it recorded the four biggest claims in its history. It incurred $2 million in claims during the quarter, three in Minnesota and one in Missouri.

RTW, which provides employers with workers' compensation management services, reported fourth quarter earnings of $0.13 a share, down from $0.20 a year ago and below analysts' expectations of about $0.21.
For all of 1996, RTW earned $0.73 a share, up from $0.64.

Because of the higher claims, the company increased to $1,040,000 from $450,000 its excess of loss reinsurance limit. As a result, RTW took a charge to claim and claim settlement expenses of $1.5 million in the fourth quarter.

As a result of the disappointing quarter, Piper Jaffray analyst John Penshorn lowered his 1997 earnings estimate on RTW to $0.60 a share from $0.96, but maintained a strong buy on the stock. Dain Bosworth analyst Chris Sergeant cut his rating on RTW to hold from buy, and lowered his 1997 earnings estimate to $0.54 a share from $1.00.
Despite the fourth-quarter setback, Prosser said, "We're not having a problem creating demand or a market for our services."
He said RTW's Michigan office, opened in October, is performing strongly and the Massachusetts office is likely to open during the second quarter of 1997.
"Our commitment is to grow revenues by 25 percent and maintain 14 percent after-tax profit. That's our history, that's where we've been," Prosser said.
Prosser said a senior manager is being transferred to Denver, where RTW was understaffed, to manage the claims side of the business.
He said the manager would be on-site within three weeks.
